## My thinking

I'm 70 now. My wife passed a few years back, kids went off to the city long time ago — my daughter's in Shijiazhuang, son's further. Just me in the house. Pension comes every month, daughter sends some money when she can, rest I make from the land. Ten mu and a bit — not much, but at my age it's plenty to keep my back sore.

Been doing the same rotation most of my life. Maybe seven mu or so I keep in wheat then maize right after — that's how everyone around here does it, that's how I learned from my father. The other three mu I keep in cotton. I know cotton, my wife's family always grew it, and the land on that side is a bit sandier so it suits cotton better than grain. I thought about giving up cotton — too much work picking — but my daughter says she'll come back for a week or two in autumn to help me, and the cotton money buys her children's school things, so I keep doing it.

**The wheat** — I already put it in back in October, the way I always do. Before planting I spread two bags of fertilizer per mu, one bag of compound stuff and one bag of urea saved for later. Everyone around here uses those big bags, 40 jin each... no wait, 80 jin, 40 kilos. The shop owner tells me what to buy, I just ask for the same as last year. Wheat came up fine before the cold. I watered it once before the ground froze. Now it's warming up, soon I'll top-dress the urea when it greens, and water it. Before harvest I'll water one more time if it doesn't rain at heading. Each watering from the well costs electric money, twenty-some yuan a mu maybe, I don't do it more than I need. For weeds I spray once in spring. If aphids come bad I spray one time, otherwise leave them.

Combine comes through in June, the man charges by the mu, he does the whole village in a few days. I'll get maybe eight hundred jin per mu — 400 kilo — that's a decent year. Some years I've had more, some less. Can't worry too much.

**The maize** — right behind the wheat combine, same day or next day, I get the man with the no-till planter to put the seed in. No time to plow, the straw gets chopped up fine by the combine. Buy hybrid seed from the shop, whatever they push that year, costs fifty yuan a mu or so. One bag of compound at planting, then when the maize is knee-high I put half a bag of urea if it looks yellow. Summer usually brings rain — if June-July is dry I'll water one time at tasseling, otherwise no watering. Spray once for weeds early. Pick end of September, hire the harvester man again. 

**The cotton** — this is the work. Plant mid-April when the ground's warm enough. I buy Bt cotton seed from the shop, that one the bollworms don't eat so much — been buying it for many years now. Plow the land myself with the small tractor, my neighbor comes to help. One bag compound before planting, one bag urea when it starts flowering. Water twice in summer. Spray three or four times — aphids, those green bugs, whatever comes. That's the expensive part. Then August, September, October, I pick a bit every few days, my daughter comes down for ten days in October to help me get through the heavy picking. Some seasons are good, some bad — last year we got maybe 500 jin per mu seed cotton, year before was worse because of that rain at the wrong time.

**Money** — I don't have much cash to put out up front. Sell last year's grain in spring to buy the fertilizer. Keep a couple thousand yuan aside for medicine and emergencies — at seventy you never know when something hits. If I had more money maybe I'd put more fertilizer, but I do what I've always done, it's been enough.
